text_blocks.snippet: Most residential roof replacements in Utah take [Highlight start] 1 to 3 days [Highlight end] of actual installation work, though complex roofs, specialty materials, and weather can extend the timeline .

list.snippet: Asphalt shingles: 1 to 2 days for most standard or moderately sized roofs; larger or steep roofs may take up to 3 days.
Metal roofing: 3 to 5 days, depending on panel type and roof complexity.
Tile (concrete or clay): 3 to 7 days due to heavier handling and fitting requirements.

text_blocks.snippet: What Affects the Timeline in Utah

list.snippet: Roof size and complexity: Steep pitches, multiple valleys, dormers, or skylights slow down tear-off and installation.
Decking repairs: Replacing rotted or damaged plywood decking uncovered during tear-off adds extra time.

Weather and season: Snow, high winds, rain, and freezing temperatures can pause work or delay scheduling—especially in mountain and high-elevation areas like Heber City and the Wasatch Back during late fall and winter.

Scheduling and insurance: Booking a crew during peak storm or construction seasons can add days or weeks before work starts, and insurance claims may also affect start dates. For more context on local scheduling and re-roof timelines, see this Yelp discussion on Utah re-roof projects.

text_blocks.snippet: If you share your roofing material, approximate home size, and whether you're planning to start soon or in the spring , I can give you a better sense of what to expect.
